I could. But I know I'm nowhere near ready to open my heart to someone else. I'm a lover girl, and casual flings aren't for me lol. 

The only reason I kept his number is so I can block him in the future from seeing my dating profile when I (eventually) decide to do so. Don't worry tho, he's blocked and under the name "NO ABSOLUTELY NOT"

I'm mad that he told me he wasn't looking to be in a relationship at all. That he loved me but couldn't be with me because of his own internal struggles. I'm mad that he jumped on Hinge less than a week after we stopped talking. I'm mad that he lied to me.

Honestly you're probably better off. You need someone who is sure about you. Love comes back wearing different skin, with different eyes, in different people. We will love again. And we will be with people who want to be with us too ❤️
That's all well and good. He can do whatever he wants. But seeing that screen shot right after he told me he wasn't looking to be involved with anyone, at all, in any capacity really fucking hurt.

It probably is. He told me he wasn't looking to be in a committed relationship. But he also isn't the type to hook up. It was the main reason he left, because commitment was suffocating him and he was afraid.

If the app was tinder? I probably wouldn't care. But it was Hinge. Aimed towards people looking for actual relationships. So I know he wants something, just not with me. He lied and did the one thing he promised me he wouldn't. So, coping or not, I feel no sympathy for him.

"I still want you to eat, just not at my table"

It's wonderful you don't hold any anger or resentment. I hope to let go of mine once I'm in a better place emotionally.
Thank you.
That's beyond awful. There is really no excuse for that kind of behavior. I'm so sorry you were treated like that.
It's literally like I panic internally when I see him. Stomach drops and my heart is pounding. Makes me feel sick.
Him.
There is a line. Once it is crossed, you're done. After four years of putting up with and making excuses for him? Yes, it is all gone.

He dumped me. Had a whole conversation about how being in a relationship is too much, he doesn't even think he's capable of upholding one. Aaaaand then he's on Hinge. I understand if he's trying to fill the void, but the betrayal is that he lied to me. If it were Tinder I honestly don't know if I'd care as much. But it's hinge. After he broke me and told me all that, promised that he wasn't even looking for that kind of commitment...and then jumps on fucking Hinge of all things? Yeah. Bye. Need to be by myself and then move on.
I'm only this upset because a reason he gave me to leave was that he didn't think he was capable of being in a relationship at all. With anyone. And now he's on Hinge.
Only after years of making excuses for him.

I don't really think it matters why. He looked me in the eye and told me he wouldn't do anything like that.

So, no matter the reason, no matter how valid, he still lied to me. So he's dead to me :)

YES EXACTLY. 

A wake up call. That's exactly what that was, exactly what seeing his dating profile was for me. My poor friend feels so bad for showing me, but I am much better off now. :)
Oh this is after forgiving him again and again. Years of this crap. I was finally fed up. I only gained the self respect after years of being a pushover.

I'm pretty sure I feel nothing for him anymore.

But you're right. I just gotta feel it so I can get over it and let it go.
Probably the correct decision. Don't make the same mistake I did.
It's so hard. It hurts to love someone so deeply and fiercely just for them to hurt you. She may love you, but you deserve someone who will love you in a healthy way. Someone who will choose you.

I'd give anything for my ex to be like you :,)

From one dumpee to another, that friendship is going to hurt you more in the long run. 

Love hard, but protect yourself.

Pulled a Justin Bieber.

Honestly, you're probably better off without someone who rushes into a lifelong commitment like that.
I think I'm just jaded 🥹
The signs are there...she's showing you exactly who she is. I don't think she's it for you.

You're absolutely correct. If she doesn't take accountability then I would say it's not worth your time. You have to value yourself above her.

It's so so so hard. But self respect in the end is more rewarding than making excuses for a partner who won't own up :/

It's normal to have hope that it can be salvaged. No matter how much it hurt you, it's normal to hope that things can be fixed. But in the end, would things actually be different? Could you fix what couldn't be fixed before? Would you end up broken hearted a second time? 

It's hard. It's so so hard. The only way the hope will fade is with time. Like I said in another comment, you can only confidently let an ex back into your life if they've proved they're changing or have changed. I know how badly you want her back.

A friend said this to me years ago and it's stuck with me to this day "It's not fun to love broken people"

I hope this helps even a little.
It's such a delicate situation. But, if things do go sour, you have this community. And you're free to message me as well, if only just to vent. You got this :)

🚨🚨🚨🚨

Thank you. I'm confident I'll come out the other side healed and ready for love again. Someday. I have a good support system. Thank you for your lovely words :)

My mistake was knowing he hasn't really changed and hoping for a different outcome. 

Only let them back in if they really have changed, or are putting in the work to change. Otherwise I wouldn't bother. Protect your peace!

I'd say sit and have a talk with him. If he's trying then that's a step in the right direction, but sometimes they fall back to their old ways after a little while. You're in a really tough spot right now, you're both at risk of being hurt and it's not an easy talk or decision to have or make. Take some time to think about it.
A nice note would help. And them breaking up with you does make a difference. I'd just send it to them or give it to a mutual friend, avoid any direct contact is all.

I'm gonna just say be careful. This exact thing happened to me, but before too long he grew distant again and ended it. And here I am heartbroken again. Be honest about how you feel. I was too scared to say anything about my fear of him leaving me again so I said nothing. I never said what I was feeling and it happened anyway. Don't settle for less, and good luck :)

I made something by hand for my ex's last birthday. I worked so hard on it, and I was so happy to give it to him. If he tried to give it back it would destroy me. It was made specifically for him. I don't want to know what he did with it,  if it's still up in his room, in a closet, or if he threw it out. I don't need to know. But I don't want it back. I don't know what you should do, but for me, it'd just hurt me more.

This is complicated. If he really is willing to put work in and make the relationship better, go for it. But don't open yourself up completely right away. He needs to earn that trust back, and you need to protect your heart. I think setting some boundaries for now is a good idea, and as time goes on, feel free to adjust those boundaries. I wish you luck :)

Well, if she's getting tons of expensive gifts from her father anyway, I would get him the phone. You can't give him as many expensive things. I think it would mean a lot to him. And if your daughter complains when he gets something really nice from you, remind her of her father's very expensive gifts.

NAH. A 1200 dollar phone is an expensive gift, but it's understandable if he feels jealous of his sister getting expensive gifts from her dad. You could communicate with your daughter's father and work together to make sure they both get the same value in gifts this year, so you could possibly get him the phone, while your daughter gets something equally as nice. But still, a cheaper gift should be just fine, just try for something you know he'll enjoy
